chunks: With this chain of narration, from Al-Hasan, from Abu al-Ma'za, from Dharih al-Muharibi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever recites Surah Ha Mim (Sajdah), it will be for him a light on the Day of Judgment extending as far as his eye can see, and a source of joy. He will live in the world praised and envied (or blessed with good fortune).'

key_terms.حَم السَّجْدَهَ: Surah Ha Mim (Sajdah), the 41st chapter of the Quran
key_terms.مَدَّ بَصَرِهِ: Extending as far as the eye can see, indicating vastness
key_terms.نُوراً: Light, symbolizing guidance and illumination in the afterlife

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly rewards for reciting Surah Ha Mim Sajdah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-Amal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) linking the recitation of Surah Ha Mim al-Sajdah to both worldly honor (being praised and blessed) and otherworldly radiance on the Day of Resurrection. This dual benefit reflects the Surah’s thematic emphasis on divine revelation and the prostration of believers, reinforcing its status as a source of spiritual illumination in Shia devotional practice.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) said, “One who recites Surah Ha Mim Sajdah this Surah would be a cause of happiness for him on the Day of Judgment and it would provide him such a light, which will be present as long as an eye can see. He would have a good life in this world and would be loved by others.”
